revision_note: v1.1 after independent equivalence review: F03 rewritten to remove retailer-recall contamination (double-barreled 'where + which brands'), F04 rewritten to add explicit purchase intent, F05 rewritten to add the India anchor to both versions and align plural number. Skincare block unchanged. Cells collected under v1.0 for F03/F05 were discarded before analysis.
design_rules: Every prompt is purchase-intent (the user is deciding what to buy), not informational.
No brand names appear in any prompt: this measures unaided brand recall of the engine.
Each EN/HG pair holds intent, category, constraints (price cap, gender, market) identical; only the language register changes.

Hinglish versions are romanized Hindi-English code-mix as typed by real Indian users: category nouns stay in English (face wash, sunscreen, jeans), function words and verbs in romanized Hindi. No Devanagari.
Price caps written as '₹N' in English and 'N rupees' in Hinglish, matching how each register is actually typed. Documented as a naturalism-over-literalism decision.
India is explicitly anchored in every prompt so market context is constant across engines.
Idiomatic mappings are deliberate, not drift: 'acne wali skin' renders 'acne-prone skin' (S05); a literal calque would be the machine-translation tell.
